strengths: Comprehensive and principled data scaling: The paper systematically curates an 8.5M spatial instruction tuning dataset (SenseNova-SI-8M) mapped to a clear taxonomy of spatial capabilities (Metric Measurement, Spatial Relations, Mental Reconstruction, Perspective-taking, and Comprehensive Reasoning), addressing critical data scarcity particularly in perspective-taking.

Strong and consistent empirical performance: SenseNova-SI achieves state-of-the-art results across five diverse spatial benchmarks (VSI-Bench, MMSI, MindCube, ViewSpatial, SITE) across multiple model backbones (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, Bagel) while preserving general multimodal reasoning capabilities on MMBench-En.

Rigorous shortcut and bias analysis: The authors perform thorough sanity checks, including blind evaluations without visual inputs, circular option-order testing, and evaluation on VSI-Debiased, convincingly showing that performance gains stem from genuine spatial understanding rather than textual priors or memorization.

Insightful analysis of CoT and emergent transfer: The paper offers valuable observations, such as cross-task capability spillover (e.g., from ego-exo alignment to maze pathfinding), frame extrapolation beyond training length, and an honest, critical study demonstrating the current limitations of text-based Chain-of-Thought for spatial reasoning.
Downstream robotic validation: Zero-shot evaluation on EmbodiedBench demonstrates tangible benefits of enhanced spatial representations for downstream embodied manipulation tasks.
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: The methodology relies primarily on data aggregation, synthesis, and standard supervised fine-tuning on existing multimodal backbones without proposing new model architectures, spatial inductive biases, or novel training objectives.

Insufficient details on synthetic data generation and quality filtering: While data sources (e.g., ScanNet++, Ego-Exo4D, MessyTable) are listed, the exact generation pipelines, prompting templates, coordinate normalization, quality verification, and filtering mechanisms used to construct the 4.5M new samples are not described in sufficient detail.

Preliminary nature of the CoT investigation: The exploration of Chain-of-Thought is restricted to a single sub-task (VSI Object Relative Direction) with simple SFT formats; claims about the limitations of CoT for spatial intelligence would be much stronger if evaluated across more diverse tasks or alongside test-time search / reinforcement learning methods.

Reproducibility details: Model and code repository placeholders on the front page are left blank, and exact training compute configs/hyperparameter sensitivities across different architectures are only briefly covered.

strengths: Comprehensive empirical study and data scaling: Curating and unifying an 8.5M QA dataset (SenseNova-SI-8M) structured along a clear five-part taxonomy (MM, SR, MR, PT, CR), providing a strong open foundation for spatial intelligence research.

Strong experimental performance: SenseNova-SI variants consistently achieve state-of-the-art results across five diverse spatial benchmarks (VSI-Bench, MMSI, MindCube, ViewSpatial, SITE), outperforming prior open-source models and several proprietary baselines while preserving general multimodal capabilities on MMBench-En.

Rigorous shortcut and bias evaluation: The paper conducts thorough sanity checks against language shortcuts, including circular evaluation tests, zero-vision ablation on MindCube, and validation on VSI-Debiased, convincingly showing that performance gains stem from visual-spatial grounding rather than memorization or text biases.

Valuable diagnostic analyses: The paper provides candid and insightful explorations into frame extrapolation (training on 16 frames while extrapolating to 32/64 frames), task spill-over, and an objective evaluation of spatial Chain-of-Thought (CoT) revealing the limitations of standard text-based CoT for spatial reasoning.
Downstream robotic validation: Successfully demonstrates zero-shot transfer to robotic manipulation on the EmbodiedBench benchmark, showing practical utility for embodied AI.
weaknesses: Lack of detailed data synthesis and quality control protocols: While Section 3.2 lists the source 3D datasets (MessyTable, ScanNet, CA-1M, Ego-Exo4D, etc.), the paper provides insufficient procedural detail regarding prompt templates, heuristic filtering, annotation pipelines, and verification metrics used to construct the 4.5M newly synthesized samples.

Limited evaluation on general multimodal benchmarks: Retention of general vision-language competence is measured almost solely on MMBench-En. Evaluating across a broader spectrum (e.g., MathVista, DocVQA, MMMU, HallusionBench) would more comprehensively rule out subtle catastrophic forgetting across different domains.

Preliminary CoT investigation: Although the negative/modest findings regarding spatial CoT are realistic, the study is restricted to 100K training examples on a single subtask (Object Relative Direction), leaving open whether other structured intermediate representations (e.g., program-based or visual sketch tokens) could unlock CoT benefits.

Reproducibility considerations: Full pretraining from scratch requires significant compute (128 GPUs for 3 days per model); open-sourcing the full dataset processing pipeline, filtering scripts, and data splits will be crucial for complete verification.

strengths: State-of-the-art performance across diverse benchmarks: SenseNova-SI achieves substantial gains on five recent spatial benchmarks (VSI-Bench, MMSI, MindCube, ViewSpatial, and SITE), consistently outperforming prior specialized models (such as Cambrian-S, VST, and SpatialLadder) as well as leading proprietary foundation models, while preserving general vision-language capabilities on MMBench-En.

Principled and comprehensive data curation: Guided by a rigorous spatial taxonomy, the authors curate an 8.5M dataset (SenseNova-SI-8M) covering five core spatial capabilities, with dedicated scaling in previously underrepresented domains such as perspective-taking and allocentric transformations.

Thorough diagnostics and shortcut analyses: The paper provides commendable empirical diligence against language shortcuts and overfitting by evaluating on debiased benchmarks (VSI-Debiased), vision-ablation tests (confirming true visual dependency vs. prior models that retained ~50% accuracy blindly), and circular option permutations.

Valuable analytical findings and negative results: The manuscript offers insightful observations on cross-task capability spill-over (e.g., ego-to-exo viewpoint training transferring to maze pathfinding), temporal context extrapolation beyond the 16-frame training budget, and an informative critical assessment of text-based spatial Chain-of-Thought (CoT) indicating that text CoT yields limited improvements over direct data scaling.
Downstream embodied validation: Demonstrates zero-shot transfer utility to robotic manipulation tasks on EmbodiedBench, showing practical applicability beyond standard VQA benchmarks.
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: The core contribution is almost exclusively data-centric. While scaling and data curation are practically impactful, the work adopts standard pretraining/fine-tuning recipes on off-the-shelf foundation models (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, Bagel) without introducing novel model architectures, spatial tokens, or specialized geometric objectives.

Data generation and quality control details are sparse: Although the paper states that 4.5M QA pairs were newly synthesized from raw 3D datasets (e.g., ScanNet, ScanNet++, Ego-Exo4D, Matterport3D), the precise prompting templates, rule-based heuristics, 3D annotation extraction pipelines, and automated filtering/verification protocols are only briefly summarized in Section 3.2.

Potential risk of scene-level dataset contamination: Multiple spatial benchmarks (such as VSI-Bench, SITE, MindCube) derive from public indoor 3D datasets like ScanNet and Matterport3D. While the paper touches upon cross-task transfer, it lacks an explicit audit verifying scene-level separation between the 8.5M training corpus and the evaluation benchmarks to completely rule out memorization of specific 3D environments.

Scope of the spatial CoT evaluation: The Chain-of-Thought investigation is restricted to a single subset (Object Relative Direction on VSI-Bench) with a fixed 100K subset, which makes the conclusion that text-based CoT is ineffective somewhat preliminary.

strengths: Comprehensive and impressive empirical performance across five major spatial intelligence benchmarks (VSI-Bench, MMSI, MindCube, ViewSpatial, and SITE), consistently matching or exceeding strong baselines and proprietary systems like GPT-5.

Principled and well-structured taxonomy for spatial intelligence, addressing severe deficits in existing datasets by specifically curating underrepresented capabilities such as perspective-taking (PT) and mental reconstruction (MR).

Thorough critical analyses including shortcut and language-prior investigations (vision-free tests and circular perturbation tests in Section 5.5), frame extrapolation behavior, and cross-task transfer/spill-over.

Insightful study on Spatial Chain-of-Thought (CoT), providing valuable negative results showing that text-centric CoT and cognitive map generation offer marginal or detrimental performance compared to direct QA scaling on geometric reasoning.
Successful zero-shot transfer to an embodied robotics task (EmbodiedBench) demonstrating practical downstream utility of the spatially aligned representations.
weaknesses: Potential risk of train-test visual scene contamination: the curated 4.5M dataset is derived from popular 3D indoor datasets (e.g., ScanNet, ScanNet++, Matterport3D, Ego-Exo4D), which are also the underlying environments for several evaluation benchmarks (e.g., VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench). The paper would benefit from explicit documentation of scene-level splits ensuring that no test environments were seen during training.

Limited architectural novelty: the approach relies strictly on standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) across existing multimodal foundation architectures (InternVL, Qwen-VL, Bagel), making the contribution predominantly centered on data curation and empirical findings.

The evaluation of Spatial CoT (Table 4) is conducted solely on a single subset of VSI-Bench (Object Relative Direction); evaluating across a broader range of spatial tasks would strengthen the generalizability of the conclusion regarding the limitations of textual CoT in spatial domains.

strengths: Comprehensive empirical investigation: The paper conducts an extensive study on scaling spatial intelligence across three diverse multimodal foundation architectures (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, and Bagel), validating that structured data scaling yields substantial improvements across diverse model families.

Well-structured taxonomy and dataset curation: The paper addresses key gaps in existing spatial datasets (specifically perspective-taking and mental reconstruction) by systematically constructing SenseNova-SI-8M (4M open-source + 4.5M newly curated pairs from 3D datasets such as ScanNet++, Ego-Exo4D, and Matterport3D).

State-of-the-art results: SenseNova-SI sets new benchmarks across five recent spatial evaluation suites (VSI-Bench, MMSI, MindCube, ViewSpatial, and SITE), outperforming prior dedicated spatial models and matching/exceeding proprietary baselines on several subtasks, while preserving general vision-language capabilities (e.g., on MMBench-En and MMStar).

Rigorous shortcut and bias analysis: The authors conduct crucial sanity checks—including evaluating against VSI-Debiased, testing performance without visual input on MindCube, and applying soft/hard circular choice permutations—demonstrating that gains stem from grounded spatial reasoning rather than language priors.

Insightful analysis of Spatial Chain-of-Thought (CoT): The preliminary investigation into text-based spatial CoT provides valuable empirical evidence and case studies showing that textual rationalizations can accumulate geometric errors and fail to outperform simple QA scaling despite massive token overhead.
weaknesses: Limited architectural and algorithmic novelty: The work primarily follows a data-centric supervised fine-tuning (SFT) recipe on existing base models without introducing novel model architectures, loss formulations, or specialized spatial representation modules.

Reproducibility of data generation: While Appendix B outlines high-level filtering rules (connectivity, visibility, angle ambiguity), the precise prompt templates, heuristic code details, and complete generation pipelines used to produce all 4.5M synthetic QA pairs from raw 3D point clouds and meshes could be more fully documented.

Diminishing returns and lack of next-step solutions: While the paper honestly notes performance saturation as data scales toward 8M and concludes that data scaling alone cannot reach human-level spatial intelligence, it provides limited concrete architectural or learning-paradigm solutions to overcome this saturation barrier.

strengths: Comprehensive and principled spatial taxonomy: The paper addresses key spatial intelligence deficits by curating SenseNova-SI-8M (8.5M QA pairs), with systematic categorization across Metric Measurement, Spatial Relations, Mental Reconstruction, Perspective-Taking, and Comprehensive Reasoning, specifically mitigating the historical underrepresentation of perspective-taking.

State-of-the-art empirical performance: Across multiple diverse benchmarks (VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench, MindCube, ViewSpatial, SITE), the SenseNova-SI models establish strong open-source SoTA results across different backbones (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, Bagel), in some subtasks even rivaling or outperforming proprietary foundation models like GPT-5 while preserving general multimodal capabilities (e.g., on MMBench-En and MMStar).

Thorough evaluation of shortcuts and robustness: The authors conduct critical analyses regarding benchmark exploits, evaluating on VSI-Debiased, running blind 'no-vision' ablation on MindCube, and performing circular permutation tests on options. These experiments demonstrate that the model genuinely grounds spatial decisions in visual input rather than exploiting spurious linguistic biases.

Insightful exploration of Spatial Chain-of-Thought (CoT): Rather than presenting only positive claims, the paper provides an honest, critical study on text-based and cognitive-map CoT schemes (Tab. 4, Appendix H), revealing that linear auto-regressive verbal rationalization is prone to early error accumulation and does not reliably outperform direct QA scaling for geometry-heavy tasks.
Practical embodiment evaluation: The zero-shot evaluation on EmbodiedBench demonstrates clear downstream benefits to robotic manipulation planning without task-specific fine-tuning.
weaknesses: Limited architectural innovation: The work is fundamentally data-centric and relies on existing model architectures (InternVL3, Qwen3-VL, Bagel) with standard supervised fine-tuning objectives, without introducing novel inductive biases or architectural mechanisms for 3D spatial representation.

Potential scene overlap and dataset contamination analysis: While the authors evaluate transfer across tasks and datasets, several underlying 3D environments (e.g., ScanNet, ScanNet++, Matterport3D) are common across both pretraining sources and existing spatial benchmarks (such as VSI-Bench). A more explicit discussion or audit of scene/split overlap between training assets and evaluation benchmarks is needed to rule out scene-level memorization.

Context window and temporal frame degradation: The models are trained on at most 16 frames per sample. While extrapolation to 32 and 64 frames shows reasonable zero-shot capability, performance degrades when extending to 128 frames (Tab. 2), showing clear context-scaling boundaries compared to models trained directly on long video contexts.

Missing release links in submission: The code and model links in the abstract and main text are left blank as placeholders; detailed specifications of data generation prompts and pipelines will be essential for full community reproducibility.
